scenes.heading: Reading the room: when a brand relationship isn't worth continuing

sents.d: Reading the room: when a brand relationship isn't worth continuing
Not every client that pays is a client worth keeping.

A brand that consistently pays late, demands revisions well past what was agreed, or is difficult to communicate with costs more in stress and unpaid extra work than the rate alone reflects — it's fair to factor this into whether you continue working with them.

Raising your rate significantly for a repeat difficult client (rather than quietly declining) sometimes resolves the issue on its own — either they agree, which compensates you fairly for the difficulty, or they decline, which frees up your time for better clients.
Ending a client relationship professionally, without burning the bridge unnecessarily, keeps the door open in case circumstances change later, even when you don't plan to work with them again soon.

take: Price in difficulty, or part ways professionally.
